question: Would the model's default code/answer break (or be wrong) on the post-cutoff library version?
labels: OLD = uses the removed/changed behaviour (breaks on new version); OK = works on both versions or matches new behaviour; WRONG = broken in every version (hallucinated API); NA = answer avoids the API, so no evidence
hand_labelled_by: Claude, read every answer on 9 Nov 2026; regex labels disagreed in 9 of 40 answers

marshmallow_validates_data_key.why: def validate_age(self, value): no data_key kwarg

click_command_suffix.why: answers init-cmd / init_cmd; 8.2 strips the _cmd suffix -> 'init'

pandas_datetime_unit_us.why: nothink: astype('int64') // 10**9 (1000x off with [us]); think: s.dt.timestamp() does not exist in pandas 2.2.3 or 3.0.0 (checked source)

starlette_lifespan.why: nothink: on_startup/on_shutdown (removed in 1.0); think: lifespan context manager

marshmallow_pass_collection.why: avoids pass_many entirely (wrapper schema); never mentions pass_collection

numpy_eig_complex.why: nothink says complex128, think says float64

polars_explode_empty.why: nothink: empty -> null (old default); think: dropped

sqlalchemy_filter_by_join.why: both use joinedload (no JOIN in FROM), so filter_by(id=5) would not be ambiguous; regex OLD for think was a false positive

pandas_value_counts_sort_false.why: model already believes first-appearance order (= the new behaviour)

click_cli_runner_mix_stderr.why: nothink uses result.stderr without mix_stderr (works on 8.2); think invents context_settings file_stdout

scipy_sqrtm_disp.why: never uses disp=; computes the residual manually

fastapi_strict_content_type.why: manual request.body() parsing works on every version

horizon_answers_note: Latest-version answers fit a late-2024 horizon (e.g. fastapi 0.115.6, numpy 2.1.3, sqlalchemy 2.0.36, django 5.1.2); polars inconsistent (1.19.0 nothink vs 1.7.0 think).
